summary.tldr: Bans ads for certain high sugar, high salt or high fat foods that are mainly aimed at children under 13.
what_it_does: Prohibits advertising prescribed foods, set by regulation, that exceed prescribed levels of sugars, saturated fat or sodium, when the ads are primarily directed at children under 13.
Protects trademark registrations by saying compliance with this ban does not make a trademark invalid or count as non-use under the Trademarks Act.
Requires a parliamentary committee review before the fifth anniversary of the new rules, including whether advertising shifts toward people aged 13 to 17.
Lets regulations set the factors for deciding when advertising is mainly directed at children, limit the kinds of advertising covered, and define “sugars” and “saturated fat”.
Brings the act into force on a day fixed by the Governor in Council.
summary.background: The bill amends the Food and Drugs Act by adding new rules on advertising directed at children. It also gives regulation-making powers for how the ban will work.
